subject: TELEPHONE FRAUD - SAMPAGUITA STREET / TERMINAL ROAD
paragraphs: The barangay has forwarded eleven complaints this month, all describing the same kind of call. A fraud desk. A support line. A prize office. A recruiter. Someone with a reason you have to act now and a reason you cannot hang up and check. Some of the complainants paid. Most did not report it until a neighbor did.
Nobody has a name. What they have is a voice, a script and a number, and the number goes to a floor of desks somewhere in this district.

Your job is to find the people who answered those calls and get their statements on record. A statement is what turns a complaint into a case. Enough of them and someone on that floor will have to answer for what is printed on his script - and whoever hands him the script will have to answer for that.
A case holds {statements} statements. Spend them on the people who will talk.

Most of the people on that list will not talk to a stranger. They will talk to someone who has already helped a neighbor. That is credibility, and it moves:
• A statement that holds up raises it. A half statement raises it less.
• An interview that goes wrong lowers it, and that witness will not open the door again.
• Reading a caller's tactic right earns a little. Reading it wrong costs a little.
• A door that stays shut costs nothing and earns nothing. The number each door needs is on the People page.
Listen for what the callers did, not only what they took. The tactics are the evidence.
prologue_note: Some of the complaints came in overnight, from people who kept the number and called it in.
closing: Start on Sampaguita Street, with whoever will open the door. Terminal Road is down the second side street.
